clue.text: Try to deal with getting two different animals back

indicators.note: getting the animals back means the pair is read from right to left

parts.note: an elk is a large deer
a cat is a common pet

explanation.surface: A farmer struggles when two strays wander home together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the whole run ELKCAT, the two animals side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To tackle a problem is to set about handling it.

clue.text: Knobbly pipe came up

parts.note: a tube is a pipe
rose means came up, like the sun

explanation.surface: A gnarled length of piping surfaced unexpectedly.
explanation.walkthrough: The plant name doubles as an adjective, a rare variant of tuberous.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means tuberous, covered in lumps and swellings.

clue.text: I guarantee my acquaintance has done well

definitions.text: I guarantee my acquaintance has done well

parts.words: I guarantee my acquaintance has done well
parts.note: read as the words of someone in court vouching for the good name of a person they know

explanation.surface: Someone proudly vouches that a friend has made good.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like pride in a friend's success; in court, 'done well' means behaved well.
explanation.definitionFit: A person called in a trial to speak to the defendant's good reputation.

clue.text: Meadow flower's first appearance?

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow

indicators.note: first signals the opening letter of the word flower's

explanation.surface: The first bloom to show itself in a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the question mark: a plant's first appearance above ground is its leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Foliage is how a plant shows itself, so a leaf is a plant's visible form.

clue.text: The state of an old ship with a new military force

parts.note: the ark is Noah's ancient vessel
the SAS is the Special Air Service, a British special forces regiment

explanation.surface: A nation's identity told through a veteran vessel and fresh troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state in the South, capital Little Rock.

clue.text: Rationed out nibbles for those in this class

definitions.text: nibbles for those in this class

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Snacks are handed out sparingly to a group of pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges RATIONED; the definition describes gnawing animals, the order of mammals named for their teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: The order of mammals that gnaw, including rats and mice.

clue.text: I assume Ann is involved as type of 17

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters are tangled up together

explanation.surface: Someone guesses Ann has a hand in some typing job.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is SECRETARY (part of 20 across); 'involved' rearranges the ten letters of I ASSUME ANN.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerk who writes from dictation is a kind of personal assistant.

clue.text: One in bed's got up to see old philosopher

indicators.note: in a down entry, got up means read from the bottom upwards
in places one item inside another

parts.note: cots are small beds
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone rises from bed to visit an ancient thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I inside COTS to make COITS, which 'got up' turns upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Zeno's ancient Greek school, which taught calm endurance.

clue.text: Study turf first -it's very wet

indicators.note: first tells us the turf piece comes before the study

parts.note: a sod is a piece of turf
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: Someone researching lawns gets soaked doing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Soaked through, as with rain.

clue.text: Across Good-natured acquaintance not cultivated

parts.note: describes a kind-hearted person lacking polish, likened to an uncut gem

explanation.surface: A friendly sort who never learned the social graces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Across' at the start is the leftover cross-reference to 11 across, not part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone decent at heart but unrefined, like a gem not yet cut.

clue.text: Underwear starts fuss, after very bold display

indicators.note: starts says the underwear piece begins the answer
after places the fuss piece behind the very piece

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear
ado means fuss

explanation.surface: A row over lingerie follows a brazen show.
explanation.definitionFit: Swagger meant to impress, a show of daring.

clue.text: See 9
Best forget about a lot of papers

indicators.note: forget tells us to drop a piece from the word for best

parts.note: the cream is the best part
C is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Advice to put the finest work aside and move on.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of 500 sheets of paper, hence a large quantity.

clue.text: He may give advice — on going Dutch?

definitions.text: He may give advice — on going Dutch?

parts.words: He may give advice — on going Dutch?
parts.note: a stern adviser is a Dutch uncle, and newspaper advice columnists answer readers' problems

explanation.surface: A columnist fielding letters about splitting the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going Dutch' looks like sharing a bill; it points to the Dutch uncle, a blunt counsellor, and his newspaper cousin who answers readers' troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: A male newspaper columnist who answers readers' personal problems.

clue.text: Varying wildly, storing art up for easy profit

indicators.note: storing means holding one piece inside another
wildly suggests the letters are thrown about
in a down entry, up means read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: Prices fluctuating madly while artwork is kept in storage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' rearranges VARYING to GRAVYIN; 'up' turns ART into TRA, which 'storing' places inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A source of money gained with little effort.

clue.text: Short day where Ashes are secured-in a different world!

parts.note: Sat is the short form of Saturday
the Ashes, cricket's England–Australia trophy, is a small urn

explanation.surface: A brief cricket day spent guarding the Ashes feels otherworldly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the cricket series between England and Australia, its trophy a tiny urn.
explanation.definitionFit: Another planet, the sixth from the sun.

clue.text: See 2
See 20 across
Do this to ride, initially, in appropriate seat

definitions.text: Do this to ride, initially, in appropriate seat

indicators.note: in places the opening letters inside the seat

parts.note: a saddle is the right seat for riding

indicators.note: initially picks the first letters of to and ride

explanation.surface: Instructions for mounting a horse properly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: to ride a horse you sit astride the saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit with a leg on each side, as a rider does on horseback.

clue.text: Old landowner had endless spree, having secured status

indicators.note: having secured means holding another piece inside
endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a fling is a short spree
rank is status

explanation.surface: A squire who partied hard but held on to his position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts FLING to FLIN, which 'having secured' wraps round RANK.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval freeholder, a landholder below gentry rank.

clue.text: Down I must have confidence in the boss's personal arrangements

definitions.text: I must have confidence in the boss's personal arrangements

parts.words: I must have confidence in the boss's personal arrangements
parts.note: the speaker is an aide trusted with an executive's ... affairs

explanation.surface: An employee worries about trusting the manager's plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' at the start is the leftover cross-reference to 17 down, not part of the clue. 'Have confidence in' reads as trust, but means being trusted with secrets.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal assistant handling an executive's confidential affairs.

clue.text: One of the royals — second to get behind military movement?

indicators.note: the second letter moves to the back of the word

parts.note: a prince is a royal

explanation.surface: A royal is assigned to a back-up role on manoeuvres.
explanation.walkthrough: The R moves from second place to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A pincer movement is an attack closing on the enemy from two sides.

clue.text: A toff too!

parts.note: a swell is a smart, upper-class person, like a toff

explanation.surface: An exclamation: yet another posh chap!
explanation.walkthrough: A toff is British slang for an upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: Means also, in addition.

clue.text: See 28 across
Quibble with separate components in locks

parts.note: split means separate
locks of hair are made of hairs

explanation.surface: Arguing over the separate strands of a hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for arguing over trivial distinctions.

clue.text: Potentially fertile material reduced? Love to contribute

indicators.note: to contribute means to go into the word for reduced

parts.note: less means reduced
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Fertile soil is in short supply, so love must pitch in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to contribute' puts O inside LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Wind-blown silt that forms rich farming soil.

clue.text: Eager to participate in whaling, it's said

definitions.text: to participate in whaling, it's said

explanation.surface: A keen harpooner signs on to a whaling ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Means enthusiastic; also to wail for the dead, as at an Irish funeral.

clue.text: Fellow gets fed up, offered cheese

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: ate means fed

explanation.surface: A man, sick of eating, is offered cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ATE into ETA.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek brined white cheese made from sheep's milk.

clue.text: Down Mere lad, terribly immature, resembling one of the Stones?

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are badly jumbled

parts.note: green means immature, inexperienced

explanation.surface: A naive young man is compared to a Rolling Stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' at the start is the leftover cross-reference to 23 down. 'terribly' rearranges MERE LAD; the Stones are gemstones, not the band.
explanation.definitionFit: The bright colour of an emerald, a precious gem.

clue.text: Stare at pupil's environment

definitions.meaning: the pupil sits in the eye's globe

explanation.surface: A teacher glares at a student in class.
explanation.definitionFit: Means to look hard at; also the globe of the eye, around the pupil.

clue.text: RN delays upset Greek naval commander

indicators.note: upset suggests the letters are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Royal Navy hold-ups annoy an admiral from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges RN DELAYS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spartan admiral who won the Peloponnesian War at sea.

clue.text: Feature of landscape seen in Tuscany only

indicators.note: seen in says the letters are found inside the words

explanation.surface: A scenic sight unique to an Italian region.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep gorge, a striking natural feature.
